// diagnostic

E1011

Fixed bytes or a rest capture in a binary pattern don't start on a byte boundary (D-BINPAT1)

What

Fixed bytes or a rest capture in a binary pattern don't start on a byte boundary (D-BINPAT1)

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E1011

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1011: tests/ui/binpat_unaligned_rest.stderr.

Error [E1011]: this part of the binary pattern doesn't start on a byte boundary
  --> tests/ui/binpat_unaligned_rest.jet:4:22
    |
  4 |         [U8]{"{a:U4}{rest:...}"} -> { print("x") }
    |                      ^^^^^^^^
 Why: fixed bytes and a `{rest:...}` capture are read whole-byte, so every bit-field before them must add up to a multiple of 8 bits
 Fix: pad the preceding holes to a byte boundary (e.g. add a reserved `{_:U4}`)
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1011

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/binpat_unaligned_rest.jet:4:39
    |
  4 |         [U8]{"{a:U4}{rest:...}"} -> { print("x") }
    |                                       ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/binpat_unaligned_rest.jet:6:13
    |
  6 |             print("no")
    |             ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116
